newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weak on dlr short cover, rates.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weak on dlr short cover, rates.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended an earlier slide to close sharply weaker due to demand to cover dollar shorts and a greater-then-expected fall in primary rates, traders said.
"Several banks were short on dollars and had to buy," a trader said. "Nonetheless, trading volume was very thin."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart closed the year at 7.8850/7.8950 and 7.8750/7.8750 per dollar, respectively, 3.8 and 3.7 centavos weaker than the close on Monday.
The 48-hour and 24-hour peso had closed 1995 at 7.69/7.70 and 7.68/7.69, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.9 centavos weaker at 7.8610/7.8640 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico assigned benchmark 28-day Cetes at 25.71 percent at its primary auction on Monday night, a fall of 154 basis points since last week's auction.
A Reuters survey of nine money market traders conducted on Monday afternoon, prior to the auction, showed they were expecting an average fall of just 69 basis points.
Traders also noted the peso weakened in the wake of increased yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds, to 6.64 percent from 6.55 percent in late trade on Monday.
Mexican financial markets will be closed on Wednesday, January 1, 1997, due to the New Year holiday.
